samples.cause: The PostgreSQL database of Keycloak is unreachable: Keycloak cannot open a connection, its readiness check on the database connections reports DOWN, so the pod is not ready and the gateway has no backend. The process is alive. A restart of Keycloak does not help; the database must come back.

samples.cause: A configuration change set the option KC_PROXY_HEADERS to the invalid value xforward. Keycloak refuses to start, so the new pod is in CrashLoopBackOff, and with the strategy Recreate the old pod is already gone. A restart starts the same configuration; the change must be reverted or fixed.

samples.cause: The Keycloak container uses more memory than its limit and the kernel kills it (OOMKilled) again and again under load; the logs stop without an error because the JVM is killed. A restart does not raise the limit. The fix is a larger memory limit in the values of the pack, a change that a person approves (T2).

samples.cause: The upgrade to Keycloak 26.8.2 is migrating the database: the new pod started and logged 'Migrating older model to 26.8.2', and it reports ready only when the migration ends.
